scenes.heading: What is Batch Processing?
scenes.narration: Batch processing is a method of handling data by collecting it into groups and processing each group on a schedule rather than instantly.

scenes.heading: Characteristics of batch processing
bullets: Data is collected over a window of time
Processing runs on a schedule, like hourly or nightly
scenes.narration: In batch processing, data is collected over a window of time before anything runs. The processing then executes on a schedule, such as hourly or nightly. Grouping work this way handles very large volumes efficiently. The design prioritizes throughput and cost-efficiency rather than instant results.

scenes.heading: Batch vs stream processing
scenes.narration: Batch processing works on grouped data at scheduled intervals, delivering high throughput but higher latency. Stream processing works on data continuously as each event arrives, delivering low latency. You choose batch when timeliness can wait and efficiency at scale matters most.

scenes.heading: A batch job's lifecycle
scenes.narration: A batch job first collects incoming data into a group. It waits until its scheduled time to run. It then processes the entire batch at once and stores the results for downstream use.

scenes.text: Batch processing groups data and runs on a schedule, favoring efficient, high-volume throughput.
scenes.narration: In short, batch processing groups data and runs on a schedule, making it the efficient choice for high-volume workloads that can tolerate some delay.
